- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model tends to overcorrect; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias if sentiment is weak or flat.
